liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 review, 1 other source): Bobby sounds energized on it, a song the reviewer hadn't heard in a long while; Jerry's licks confirming the song made the uploader lose it [1][11]
- **Looks Like Rain** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls it the best version ever, with Jerry playing intensely despite his sick voice; Reviewer says it steals the show [9][10]
- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review): Opener is mellow but decently performed [11]
- **Don't Ease Me In** (1 review): Band slid into it spontaneously; Brent put his hands on his head while Jerry laughed [8]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Described as stratospheric, following a trippy Other One [18]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Reviewer found the Good Lovin' into Dear Mr. Fantasy into Hey Jude ending bizarre and enjoyable [13]
- **Dear Mr. Fantasy** (1 review): Tacked on after Good Lovin', it matched or even topped the Stella Blue peak [18]
- **Never Trust A Woman** (1 review): Reviewer calls Brent's performance an early show-stopper in the first set [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-04-04.138756.FOB.Schoeps.Bryant.Gastwirt.Miller.Noel.t-flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 140 min [1]
- **gd1988-04-04.sbd.miller.91162.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 132 min; rated 3.2/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1988-04-04.152576.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 132 min [4]
- **gd1988-04-04.152203.sbd.miller-voss-pearson-healy.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 132 min [5]
- **gd1988-04-04.aud.koucky.gmb.86913.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 130 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [6]. Said about its sound: Excellent, well-balanced audience recording [15]

## Around the show

- Jerry was sick during this run, so his singing suffered [9]
- A friend predicted before the show that a new Beatles tune would be played; Hey Jude followed [10]
- Reviewer's tenth show, first trip with Peter C.; they drove an Oldsmobile on its last Dead trip to Hartford [12]
- Jerry had a cold that dampened the show, though the music was on [12]
- Reviewer worked nearby and ate lunch in Bushnell Park among fans camping out during the run [13]
- Tie-dyes hung from the upper levels all the way around the arena [14]
- Reviewer notes Jerry's vocal problems and some dull guitar; band seemed frustrated yet energetic by the end [17]
- Jerry's voice sounded like end-of-tour hoarseness, possibly laryngitis, mid-tour [1]
- Despite Jerry's cold, reviewer sees the show as a sign of the band's upward trajectory [12]
- Reviewer's favorite of the Hartford nights, partly for the Alabama Getaway into Johnny B. Goode opening [13]
- Reviewer says Brent is starting to step forward more, and Brent and Bobby fans will enjoy it [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-04-04.138756.FOB.Schoeps.Bryant.Gastwirt.Miller.Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Robert Bryant; transferred by Charlie Miller, Rich Gastwirt, Joe Noel; source: Recorded by Robert Bryant FOB (patched out of Oade Brothers) Schoeps CMC4 MK41 > PCM > DAT; Charlie Miller [1]
- **gd1988-04-04.sbd.miller.91162.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) D [2]. Also: Dear Mr. Fantasy transfer chain: unknown mics to PCM to DAT to CD, filled in from another source; Another source (shnid 10072) supplies Don't Ease Me In seconds 17 to 56 [2]
- **gd1988-04-04.152576.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  January 16, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R) [4]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple masters were combined to complete the show; This version is a 24-bit to 16-bit conversion at 44.1 kHz of release 152203 [4]
- **gd1988-04-04.152203.sbd.miller-voss-pearson-healy.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  January 16, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R) [5]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple masters were used to complete the show; Jim Voss helped with this project [5]
- **gd1988-04-04.aud.koucky.gmb.86913.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Bill Koucky; transferred by Chris Ladner; source: Tapers section, Sennheiser ME88s > Sony D5. Master Analog Cassettes Maxell MX90 Type IV cassettes. [6]
